I'm a 31-year-old farmer with an agricultural college degree, managing 225 mu here in Quzhou County. I took over this land from my family four years ago and have been running it as a proper business since then. With 150 mu in wheat-maize double cropping and 75 mu in cotton, I need to think about cash flow and labor scheduling, not just yields.

Right now it's late April, so my winter wheat is already in the ground — I planted an improved variety in mid-October at about 12 kg per mu. I did a soil test last September: organic matter was around 1.8%, available N was on the low side, so I'm targeting about 18 kg N per mu this year. I already applied the base fertilizer back in October — 50 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) plus 5 kg urea per mu before sowing. I topdressed 10 kg urea per mu at green-up in late March, and I'm doing another 8 kg urea at jointing right now. If the flag leaves look pale in mid-May, I might add one more 5 kg shot, but only if the crop actually needs it — I'm not throwing money away. I've irrigated twice already, winter and green-up, and I'll do jointing irrigation this week plus one more at grain filling if May stays dry. Pumping runs about 30 yuan per mu per round, so four irrigations means I'm spending 120 yuan per mu just on water, but dryland wheat around here won't push past 400 kg/mu. I'm aiming for 520 kg/mu, which I nearly hit two years ago.

For maize, the window after wheat harvest is brutally tight — sometimes five days, sometimes ten. I hire a combine for wheat and run a rotary tiller and planter right behind it. I never save maize seed; I buy fresh hybrid every year at about 88 yuan per mu. I'm planning roughly 17 kg N per mu: 40 kg of compound fertilizer (20-10-10) at planting, then 18 kg urea topdressed at big flare stage. For water, I'll irrigate twice if the summer is normal — once at seedling if June is hot, and the absolutely critical one at tasseling/silking in late July. Missing that irrigation can cost me 150 kg/mu. My target is 580 kg/mu, though last year I only got 510 because August turned dry.

The cotton on 75 mu is my price hedge. Grain markets have been jumpy, but cotton has been steadier. I'm planting a Bt hybrid in mid-to-late April with 40 kg compound fertilizer (15-15-15) base per mu, then topdressing 20 kg urea at initial flowering. Total N around 15 kg per mu. I'll irrigate twice — at flowering and peak boll. The real cost with cotton is picking labor. At 75 mu, I need hired hands for three rounds of picking at 180 to 200 yuan per day. That's not in my upfront input budget, but it's the biggest cost. I'm expecting 280 kg lint per mu if the bollworm pressure stays manageable.

The tradeoffs are everywhere. More fertilizer on wheat means higher yield but also higher risk if a late frost hits. More irrigation pushes yield but the pumping bill adds up fast on 150 mu. For maize, the minimal tillage approach saves me four days in June, but I pay more for seed and I have to watch weed pressure. I keep a cash reserve of about 25,000 yuan because a breakdown of the combine or a sudden need for extra labor can wipe out my margins. At 225 mu, I can't do everything myself — my wife helps with spraying and bookkeeping, but I rely on hired crews for harvest and cotton picking. The total upfront input cost this year is about 95,000 yuan, which is a big number, but it's what it takes to run a business farm properly.
